A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Erwin research work and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering. Some experimental descriptions conflict internally, but the substantive revisions remain identifiable.

before.justification: v1 reports original cosmology and molecular-dynamics experiments, EAGLE predictions, and ShapeNet-Car results, including the experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds PDE benchmark evaluations, ShapeNet-Car component ablations, and computational timing measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 3-4 and Appendix A retain the same ball-tree construction, attention, positional encoding, rotated-tree connections, MPNN embedding, and coarsening/refinement procedures. Coarsening-free ShapeNet configurations were already evaluated in v1 Appendix B.2; the new benchmarks do not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: v2 Section 5.3 adds Elasticity, Plasticity, Airfoil, and Pipe, substantially extending evaluation across PDE problems on point clouds and structured meshes. Cosmology, molecular dynamics, EAGLE, and ShapeNet-Car remain; ShapeNet-Car was already present in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: v2 Table 4 adds eight PDE comparators, including LNO, Galerkin, GNOT, ONO, and Transolver++. The ShapeNet comparison replaces U-Net and FNO with PointNet, Transolver, and GP-UPT while retaining GINO, UPT, and PTv3. Table 8 additionally compares tree construction against scikit-learn plus Joblib. These are reported comparisons, not merely new citations.

E3.justification: New PDE evaluations introduce specified train/test splits, relative-L2 optimization, and approximately million-parameter models. The reported global AdamW weight decay changes from 0.01 in v1 Appendix C to 0.00001 in v2 Appendix B.2; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. Tables 7-8 also introduce compiled forward/backward timing and CPU tree-construction comparison protocols.

E4.justification: ShapeNet analysis changes substantially: v1 Table 4's explicit U-Net/ResNet comparison disappears, while v2 Table 3 adds MPNN, positional-encoding, and rotated-tree component ablations. Tables 7-8 extend efficiency analysis with forward/backward timings and a tree-construction comparison. MD ablation runtimes are removed, while the cosmology ball-size ablation and appendix fluid-rollout examples are retained.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports ShapeNet means and standard deviations and states that PDE experiments used one run. Appendix B.3 specifies five runs for the other tasks; v1 already reported five for cosmology and EAGLE. However, v2 Figure 7 still says three MD runs, so the new five-run statement does not reliably establish an increase for MD.

E6.justification: New PDE results report Erwin errors of 0.34, 0.10, 2.57, and 0.61 for Elasticity, Plasticity, Airfoil, and Pipe. ShapeNet's previous Erwin/PTv3 ResNet tie at 0.92 on a stated MSE scale of 10^-2 is replaced by Erwin-S/M scores of 15.85/15.43 versus PTv3-S/M scores of 19.09/17.42. Different configurations and unexplained scales prevent direct performance comparison. New ablation and timing results are also added; the original cosmology, MD, and EAGLE headline results remain.

T1.justification: The ball and ball-tree definitions, Propositions 3.3-3.4, method equations, and Algorithm 1 retain their mathematical substance. No new proofs or formal properties appear. Appendix B.4's standard relative-L2 formula adds evaluation documentation.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list expand the claimed empirical scope to PDE solving. The conclusion adds state-of-the-art performance on a subset of standard PDE benchmarks. The central claims about hierarchical ball-tree attention, scalability, and capturing local and global interactions remain.

C2.justification: v2 introduces a speculative Airfoil failure explanation based on varying mesh density and interprets the ShapeNet ablation as showing the importance of cross-ball interactions. The limitations discussion replaces the attention-bias memory-cost warning with propagation-depth and coarsening information-loss limitations, suggesting sparse attention. It also revises proposed equivariance extensions and qualifies the advantages of learned PDE solvers over numerical methods.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the anonymized code placeholder with an explicit Erwin repository link. Expanded Appendix B documents software versions, CPU/GPU specifications, task training times, clipping, normalization, stopping rules, hyperparameter search, baseline code pointers, and PDE configurations. These are substantial documentation additions. Some remain inconsistent: ShapeNet point counts differ between Table 1 and Section 5.3, and B.7's stride-one description conflicts with Table 10's pooling values.

R1.justification: v2 substantially broadens research positioning with multiscale graph networks, Geometric Hyena, and point-cloud state-space models, alongside expanded neural-operator and PDE literature. New comparisons involve Transolver, Transolver++, and NeuralCFD-related results; future-work discussion adds Native Sparse Attention and Euclidean Fast Attention. The original attention-focused positioning is retained within this broader context.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, adopts the PTv3 abbreviation, moves ShapeNet discussion into Section 5.3, and reorganizes experimental documentation into Appendix B.1-B.7. It also adds an impact statement and revises acknowledgements. Most introductory, methodological, and original experimental prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands tabular presentation with a dataset overview, PDE results, forward/backward timings, tree-construction comparisons, and PDE architecture settings. The ShapeNet table moves into the main text and changes from U-Net/ResNet to size-based rows; the component-ablation table replaces its runtime column with ShapeNet losses. Existing figures, including appendix rollouts, retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: The added PDE tests expose an important failure case, and ShapeNet ablations clarify when cross-ball connections matter. Explicit code pointers and expanded experimental documentation also improve assessability over v1. These gains are limited by conflicting MD run counts, inconsistent ShapeNet point-count and pooling descriptions, and unexplained changes in ShapeNet score scale. The broader evidence supports a modest net improvement, with reproducibility and comparability still needing clarification.
